# Objectwise rational comparison

Synthetic local primary source supplied for forward testing; not a real publication.
Author: Synthetic Fixture Author.
Identifier: synthetic:rational-comparison.
Version: v1, dated 2026-10-02.

## Theorem 1

Let $\mathcal C$ be a category and let $A,B:\mathcal C\to\mathrm{Ab}$ be covariant functors taking values in finite-rank free abelian groups. Suppose that for each object $X$, the rational vector spaces $A(X)\otimes_{\mathbb Z}\mathbb Q$ and $B(X)\otimes_{\mathbb Z}\mathbb Q$ have the same finite dimension. For each object $X$ there exists an isomorphism of rational vector spaces between these two vector spaces.

## Proof of Theorem 1

For a fixed object, choose a basis of each rational vector space. Their dimensions are equal, so matching the basis vectors gives an invertible rational linear map. Perform this construction for each object separately.

Under the standing finite-rank and equal-rational-dimension hypotheses, there exists a natural isomorphism F=>G of integral functors.
